jobs.occupation: Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026 – Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU), Copenhagen, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Position:

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is seeking candidates for its newly established Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026. These internship opportunities are on-site at SCMU’s office in the UN City headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark.

SCMU offers specialized functional streams aligned with its operational needs, including:

• Data & Analytics

• Logistics & Supply Chain

• Procurement & Business

• Humanitarian Supplies

• Supply Chain & Customer Service

• Governance, Risk & Compliance

• Communications

• Human Resources

• Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

• Administration & Business

To ensure effective team integration and maximize the value of the internship, candidates must be logistically and financially prepared to undertake full-time, on-site work in Copenhagen for the duration of the internship.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead UN agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every childbirth is safe and every young person's potential is fulfilled.  UNFPA’s strategic plan (2026-2029), reaffirms the relevance of the current strategic direction of UNFPA and focuses on three transformative results: to end preventable maternal deaths; end unmet need for family planning; and end gender-based violence and harmful practices. These results capture our strategic commitments on accelerating progress towards realizing the ICPD and SDGs in the Decade of Action leading up to 2030. Our strategic plan calls upon UN Member States, organizations and individuals to “build forward better”, while addressing the negative impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on women’s and girls’ access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights, recover lost gains and realize our goals.

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is self-funded and was made operational in January 2022. It is tasked with ensuring that UNFPA is able to effectively and efficiently support the delivery of life-saving reproductive health products and other programme supplies to the end user when and where they are needed. To achieve this, it is important to strengthen the capacity of governments and implementing partners to ensure coordination, end-to-end visibility and accountability on all supply chain and logistics management related activities, in particular for programme supplies, across all UNFPA programmes.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff, who embody these international norms and standards, and who will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates that transform, inspire and deliver high impact and sustained results; we need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them and who commit to deliver excellence in programme results.

Eligibility:

Educational requirements

a. Be enrolled in a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent) and have completed one full academic year;

b. Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as master’s programme or higher);

c. Have recently graduated with a university degree as defined above and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation; or

d. Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional trainee programme and undertake the internship as part of this programme.

Other eligibility requirements

e. Demonstrate interest in the field of development;

f.  Demonstrate written and spoken proficiency in at least one of the working languages of the United Nations (English or French) and fluency in the official language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish) of the UNFPA office; and

g. Demonstrate ability to adapt to new environments and to establish and maintain good working relations with individuals of different cultural backgrounds.

An individual whose father, mother, son, daughter, brother or sister is a UNFPA staff member is not eligible for an internship with UNFPA.

Required Competencies:

Values:

• Exemplifying integrity,

• Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,

• Embracing cultural diversity,

• Embracing change

Core Competencies:

• Achieving results,

• Being accountable,

• Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,

• Thinking analytically and strategically,

• Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,

Financial Support:

Interns who do not receive financial support from an outside party (such as an academic institution, university, government) are eligible to receive a stipend as a contribution towards living expenses. The stipend is based on the intern’s agreed place of work, which may be different from the duty station of the hiring office in cases of remote arrangements. The stipend is normally paid in local currency at the end of each month.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA's workforce - click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants' bank accounts.

jobs.occupation: Director Specialist – Key Account Management (Power & Controls)
jobs.description:
Director Specialist – Key Account Management (Power & Controls)

Vacancy description

Director Specialist – Key Account Management (Power & Controls)

Build strategic partnerships that power the future of renewable energy

At KK Group, we are on an ambitious journey to enable a future powered by renewable energy. We are looking for a commercially driven and relationship-oriented leader to take ownership of a key strategic account and help unlock its full potential.

In this role, you will work at the heart of our business—connecting customers, technology, and operations—to drive sustainable growth, strengthen long-term partnerships, and deliver real impact.

Highlights of the offer

• Job offer expiration: 30/11/2026

• Type of work: Hybrid

• Role: Individual Contributor / Specialist

• Location: Europe, Denmark, Ikast

Responsibilities

Key Account Management:

• Obtain detailed knowledge of the account’s organization, their product portfolio, their on-going projects, and secure this is shared across commodities.

• Identify cooperation and sales opportunities

• Process customer RFQ’s and work cross-functionally with colleagues to generate the best technical and commercial offering

• Process ideas targeting increased business right from idea to implementation. Painstakingly drive the idea internally, build the business case and sell the new product or service

• Keep a strong and tight relationship with the Accounts’ technical and commercial organization and their internal stakeholders

• Contribute in development and adjustment of account strategy in order to support the overall business plan and targets for the account

• Support the customer on a day-to-day business

• Secure correct reporting, data and pipeline management in e.g. CRM

• Support all operational activities where sales need to be involved towards the customers to ensure highest level of performance.

• Drive customer negotiations to land new business and/or supporting the Key Account commodities across.

• Secure timely preparation, process and level of RFQ and negotiations across Key Account commodities and divisions.

Our requirements

We are looking for a commercially strong and collaborative professional who thrives in a global, customer-focused environment.

• 6-10 years of proven experience in Key Account Management within large OEM environments, with a proven ability to drive growth and create value for both the customer and the business

• A basic understanding of electromechanical components and industrial environments

• Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience in budgeting, performance management, and delivering on business targets

• Excellent stakeholder management and negotiation skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and align expectations across internal and external partners

• Proven experience in leading cross-functional teams and managing complex projects in an industrial or technical environment

• A structured, analytical, and data-driven mindset, enabling you to translate insights into impactful decisions

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels in a global setting

• A collaborative and inclusive leadership style, with a commitment to safety, quality, and company values

• Cross-cultural awareness and the ability to operate effectively in an international matrix organisation

• Fluency in Danish and English (written and spoken); additional languages are considered a plus

Location

This role can be based in our offices in Ikast or Hammel, with flexibility for hybrid work.

Ready to make an impact?

If you are excited about shaping strategic partnerships and contributing to the renewable energy transition, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now & send us your resume in English.

Due to the summer vacation period in Denmark, all applications will be processed only in the beginning of August.

We offer

By joining KK Group, you will be part of a culture where diversity is embraced, every nationality is respected, and trust and collaboration across perspectives drives our success. Across our global organisation, we offer a wide range of job opportunities spanning office-based roles, production facilities, and onsite positions worldwide. Our roles cover multiple functions, locations, and disciplines, providing diverse career paths across the business. Whether you’re interested in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or support functions, you’ll find opportunities at KK Group to grow your skills, contribute to meaningful work, and make an impact.

Potential Benefits (Depending on Role)

Further information

If the above matches your field of interest and your qualifications, please send your application and resume as soon as possible. Interviews are held on an ongoing basis.

For further information, please contact:

Karen Lim  +45 4194 6883

About KK Group

KK Group is a global technology partner delivering power, controls, cooling, monitoring and service solutions for renewable energy and energy-intensive industries.

With more than 45 years of experience in the wind industry and technologies installed in over 120,000 turbines worldwide, KK Group provides critical electro-mechanical systems that enable electrification, improve energy efficiency, and optimise the lifetime performance of industrial assets.

The company’s capabilities span the full value chain - from development and manufacturing to service and digital solutions - supporting customers across the entire lifecycle of their platforms. Backed by its long-term owner, A.P. Moller Holding, KK Group is expanding beyond wind into selected energy-intensive industries including hydrogen, mining, rail and defence.

Today, KK Group employs more than 3,700 people across 10+ countries and is building a more diversified, resilient and global business - Powering Change towards a more sustainable tomorrow.

Visit www.kkgroup.com to learn more about our company and career opportunities.

jobs.occupation: System Manager, AC Skid – BESS (Medium Voltage Containerized Systems)
jobs.description:
System Manager, AC Skid – BESS (Medium Voltage Containerized Systems)

Shape the backbone of the energy transition

Are you passionate about building reliable, future-ready energy systems?

Do you enjoy working at the intersection of electrical engineering, system integration, and real-world impact?

Highlights of the offer

• Job offer expiration: 30/11/2026

• Type of work: Hybrid

• Role: Individual Contributor / Specialist

• Location: Europe, Denmark

Responsibilities

Serve as the overall system‑responsible owner for the AC Skid, covering electrical/functional architecture, safety, quality, and lifecycle performance.

Lead supplier selection, qualification, and governance for the mechanical Skid design, ensuring alignment with system requirements, standards, and cost targets.

Own the technical selection and specification of:

• MV transformer

• RMU

• PCS (in house designed converter integration and interfaces

Ensure correct electrical and functional integration of all subsystems:

• MV transformer – RMU – PCS

• Grounding/earthing

• Cooling and auxiliary power

• Cabling, interlocks, protections, and monitoring

Review and validate supplier designs for the mechanical skid

Ensure compliance with relevant standards:

• MV equipment (IEC/ANSI)

• Transformer and switchgear safety

• Environmental, mechanical, and fire safety

Review supplier documentation, test results, FAT reports, and qualification data.

Drive quality and cost optimization, ensuring a price‑competitive and high‑quality AC Skid product for the BESS platform.

Support customer clarification and quotation phases, ensuring:

• Technical feasibility

• Clear interpretation of customer requirements

• Alignment between project needs and AC Skid capabilities

Collaborate cross‑functionally with electrical, mechanical, controls, product, procurement, and quality teams to ensure seamless AC Skid integration.

Our requirements

Must‑haves:

Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, Energy Engineering, or similar.

Strong understanding of:

• MV transformers, RMUs, switchgear, and MV safety

• Grid‑connected PCS/power converters

• MV protection, grounding/earthing, and interlocking

• Cooling and auxiliary systems

Experience working with suppliers on:

• Detailed mechanical design reviews

• Documentation review and compliance checks

• Quality and cost evaluations

Ability to support technical clarifications during pre‑sales and quotation phases.

Nice‑to‑haves:

Experience with AC Skids, E‑houses, containerized MV designs, or BESS systems.

Knowledge of grid code requirements for MV‑connected BESS or hybrid power plants.

Familiarity with DFMEA, FAT processes, and utility compliance documentation.

Background in system engineering or product ownership roles.

Location

This role can be based in our offices in Ikast or Hammel, with flexibility for hybrid work.

Ready to Grow Your Impact?

If you’re excited by this opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now! Send us your resume in English and help us build the energy systems of tomorrow.

Interviews will be scheduled on an ongoing basis.

jobs.occupation: System Manager, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)
jobs.description:
Vacancy description

System Manager, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)

Own the system. Shape the solution. Enable the energy transition.

Are you motivated by bringing complex energy systems together into one seamless, high-performing solution?

Do you enjoy working across technologies, teams, and disciplines to deliver real-world impact?

Highlights of the offer

• Job offer expiration: 30/11/2026

• Type of work: Hybrid

• Role: Individual Contributor / Specialist

• Location: Europe, Denmark

Responsibilities

Act as the overall system‑responsible owner of the entire BESS solution/product.

Define and maintain the system architecture, ensuring seamless integration of:

• PCS (Power Conversion System)

• Battery DC Block

• AC Skid

• EMS & Hybrid Power Plant Controller (HPPC)

• Grid interconnection & compliance

Ensure subsystem interfaces are clearly defined, robust, and fully aligned across electrical, control, mechanical, and communication domains.

Collaborate closely with other System Managers to deliver a high‑quality, reliable, safe, and easy‑to-install BESS platform.

Support customer-facing project phases, including:

• Understanding customer technical and functional requirements

• System sizing and configuration

• Defining or selecting product variants and architectures

• Clarifying integration, performance, and compliance aspects

Ensure the BESS platform meets all relevant standards and certifiable requirements for the targeted European and global markets.

Drive product-level requirement definition, functional specifications, technical governance, and change management.

Contribute to product roadmap development, ensuring alignment with market trends, grid requirements, and future hybrid power plant needs.

Support cost‑optimization, manufacturability, and quality initiatives to ensure a price-competitive product.

Maintain system documentation, design rules, product configuration guidelines, and compliance packages.

Our requirements

Must‑haves:

Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Energy Systems, Controls Engineering, or a related field.

Strong understanding of grid‑scale BESS architecture and system integration.

Experience working with multiple subsystems such as PCS, battery containers, AC Skids, and EMS/plant controllers.

Ability to define system requirements, specify subsystem interfaces, and validate system integration.

Understanding of grid interconnection requirements, certifiable standards, and BESS compliance guidelines.

Experience with customer technical discussions, system sizing, and solution definition.

Nice‑to‑haves:

Experience in hybrid power plant solutions (BESS + PV + WTG).

Familiarity with European grid codes (ENTSO‑E, national TSO/DSO requirements).

Background in product ownership, system engineering, or platform leadership.

Experience with industry certification processes for electrical or power systems.

Knowledge of thermal, mechanical, or communication aspects of BESS solutions.

Location

This role can be based in our offices in Ikast or Hammel, with flexibility for hybrid work.

Ready to take ownership of the system that powers the future?

Apply now! Send us your resume in English and help us design and deliver the next generation of battery energy storage solutions.

Interviews will be scheduled on an ongoing basis.

We help companies that cannot afford to get it wrong make better engineering design decisions. Through consulting, software and ventures, we strengthen how mechanical R&D teams think, design and deliver.

Our engineering ecosystem brings together specialist knowledge, training, documentation and software.

We work with R&D, operations and manufacturing organizations across industries, including major international companies, to make mechanical products less sensitive to variation.

What you will do

As a Robust Design Consultant, you will work directly on clients’ mechanical design challenges. You will investigate how parts interact, how tolerances affect function, and how designs can be improved.

The role combines engineering work with client dialogue and technical responsibility for project delivery.

Your background

We welcome engineers with two or more years of relevant professional experience, ideally in mechanical product development, as well as senior specialists who want to deepen their expertise and remain hands-on.

• A master’s degree in mechanical engineering or a related field.

• Strong analytical skills across mechanical function, tolerance variation, and solid mechanics.

• Knowledge of Robust Design principles.

• Knowledge of production technologies and Design for Manufacturing (DFM).

• Fluent English.

• Working knowledge of statistical methods and finite element simulation methods.

• Experience with prototyping tools and methods.

• Strong communication and presentation skills.

• Danish or German language skills.

• Advanced simulation expertise.

jobs.occupation: Hotel Allrounder (Bar, F&B, Reception all in one role)
jobs.description:
Hospitality job in Copenhagen. One role, many hats. No two days alike.  Love good coffee, great drinks and even better conversation? Want a hotel job where no day feels the same? Keep reading.   Most hotel jobs put you in one spot. At Zoku, you’ll be everywhere that matters. 

From welcoming guests and sharing local tips to serving great food, making coffee, and mixing cocktails, you’ll help create the experience people remember long after they’ve checked out. If variety is your thing and making people feel genuinely at home comes naturally to you, you might be exactly who we’re looking for. 

At Zoku, we’re not your typical hotel. We’re a community-driven space where people can live, work, socialize, and connect with the city around them. We believe hospitality should feel personal, human, and effortless and that starts with the people on our team. That’s where you come in! 

WHAT IS A SIDEKICK?  

At Zoku, we call our hospitality all-rounders “Sidekicks”. You can think of this role as a Guest Experience Host: someone who combines reception, restaurant, bar, and guest services into one dynamic hospitality role. You’re the friendly face welcoming guests at check in, the person recommending your favorite local spots, the bartender making someone’s evening, and the host creating a warm atmosphere in our rooftop Living Kitchen restaurant. 

No two days are the same and that’s exactly why people love this role. 

WHAT YOU’LL ACTUALLY DO 

Behind the bar. Pull espressos in the morning, pour craft beer in the afternoon, shake cocktails at night. We'll teach you the recipes, you bring the chat. 

In the restaurant. Serve breakfast, lunch, dinner and bites in our Living Kitchen and on our rooftop terraces with great views over the city. Guide guests to the right wine, the right small plate, the right table. 

At the front desk. Welcome arriving guests, handle check-ins & check-outs, and answer the inevitable "where's the best bakery in Copenhagen?" with the kind of tips only a local would know. 

YOUR SCHEDULE 

You’ll work independently across different departments, with both morning and afternoon/evening shifts. A standard shift is 8 hours with a 30 minute meal break. Your responsibilities and hours may vary.

• 
Morning Shift (AM Shift): 07:00 to 15:00 (+/- 1 hour)

• 
Afternoon/Evening Shift (PM Shift): 15:00 to 23:00 (+/- 1 hour)

YOU’LL FIT RIGHT IN IF YOU 

• 
Are genuinely friendly, and open. 

• 
Love creating unforgettable stays where guests feel a true sense of belonging. 

• 
Thrive in social, energetic environments. 

• 
Like variety and can easily switch between different tasks. 

• 
Are proactive, hands on, and team oriented. 

• 
Have a genuine interest in hospitality, food, drinks, travel, or community. 

• 
Love discovering and sharing the best spots in Copenhagen. 

 

A FEW MUST HAVES 

• 
You have worked in hospitality or in a similar customer-facing industry.

• 
You are fluent in English - Danish and any other languages are a big plus!

• 
You are an EU resident or have a valid working and living permit to work in Denmark.

• 
You have a CPR-number / tax number and a Danish bank account.

• 
You are flexible, as there are no fixed working days / hours and enjoy working both week days and weekends.

• 
You are available to work either 32 hours weekly (4 shifts) or 37 hours weekly (Full Time-5 Shifts).

 

Start date: We’re ready to welcome our next Sidekick as soon as possible! We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis, so don’t snooze, apply today! We’re all about finding the right match for our amazing team.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

• 
We’ll screen applications as they are submitted.

• 
We’ll give you a call to for a quick get to know each other chat.

• 
We’ll invite you in for either 1 or 2 interviews to get a tour of Zoku and meet the Team.

• 
We’ll finalize the offer and get you started!

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU 

You’ll join an international team filled with people who genuinely care about hospitality, creativity, and community. Plus, exciting training and events to celebrate every step of the journey! 

• 
A market conform salary package including pension and health insurance.

• 
A 40% discount on food & drinks for you and up to 4 friends 

• 
Discounted Employee- and Friends & Family rates across all Zoku locations (Amsterdam, Copenhagen, Vienna and Paris) 

• 
The best staff meals, enjoyed in our rooftop Social Spaces overlooking the city. 

• 
A free night stay for you and a +1 in your first 3 months – plus another free night at any Zoku location for your birthday celebration 

• 
Access to all community events, team celebrations, and after work drinks 

• 
Exciting on-the-job training opportunities and fun events throughout the year to celebrate achievements and milestones.

• 
A personal budget after your first year: spend it on extra days off, learning, or take it as cash  

Check out all benefits here.  

WHAT WE ARE PROUD OF 

Zoku combines the energy of a lifestyle brand with the warmth of a close knit team. We challenge traditional hospitality by creating spaces where people genuinely connect, whether they’re staying for one night or several months. 

Next to our award-winning design and our global press fan club, we’re proud to be a certified B Corp across all our locations, meaning we care deeply about people, community, and doing business with a heart (not just as a marketing line). 

WHAT THE ZOKU?!  We’re Zoku. Designed for the new generation of business travelers, we’re so much more than a long stay hotel. We’re a place you can call your second home, even on your first visit. We’ve created a hive of private Lofts and rooftop Social Spaces, so you can stay connected and well rested as you live and work throughout Europe. Throw yourself into your work and play, and effortlessly discover one of our home cities. It will be your home city next.  READY? Hit apply and tell us why this role has your name on it.

jobs.occupation: Treasury Analyst, Markets & Analytics
jobs.employer_name: Impact Fund Denmark (tidl. Investeringsfonden for Udviklingslande)
jobs.description:
Do you want to work in an international investment fund promoting economic and social progress through commercial investments?

Impact Fund Denmark is Denmark’s largest impact fund and is internationally recognized as a best-in-class impact investor. We manage our own private equity funds, debt capital, and concessional capital with a focus on creating sustainable businesses that deliver measurable social, economic and climate impact alongside solid financial returns.

 

About the role

We are looking for a Treasury Analyst to join our Treasury team. The role sits at the intersection of financial markets, quantitative analysis, trading and technology. You will support treasury decision-making, execute and analyse financial transactions, develop and use the tools and data infrastructure used by the Treasury function.

 

Key responsibilities

• 
Negotiate, execute and support FX, money-market, interest-rate and derivative transactions, including swaps and hedging activities.

• 
Perform quantitative analysis of FX, interest-rate and liquidity risk via statistics and scenario analyses.

• 
Develop models for cash-flow forecasting, liquidity management, pricing and risk/position management.

• 
Develop and maintain Treasury analytics and reporting using SQL, Python, Power BI and/or Excel/VBA.

• 
Extract, structure and analyse data from Treasury Risk/Position Systems, Investment Management Systems, ERP systems and market-data platforms.

• 
Automate Treasury processes and controls and contribute to improvements in the Treasury IT architecture.

• 
Support and pursue implementation and valuation of new financial products.

• 
Monitor financial markets and provide analysis supporting funding, investment and hedging decisions.

 

Qualifications

• 
Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Financial Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science or similar.

• 
Initial relevant work experience, for example 1–3 years' experience from a student job or up to 2 years full-time experience after graduation within Treasury, trading, financial markets and quantitative finance.

• 
Practical experience with FX, interest rates, derivatives and/or money-market instruments.

• 
Strong quantitative and analytical capabilities.

• 
Experience with SQL and ideally Python, VBA or similar programming languages.

• 
Understanding of databases, APIs, data structures and financial systems.

• 
Experience with Treasury Management Systems, ERP systems, Investment Management Systems and market-data platforms is an advantage. Especially Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, Microsoft Dynamics platform/data structure and Bloomberg.

• 
Ability to translate complex financial requirements into robust analytical and IT solutions.

• 
Proficiency in English is required, while spoken Danish is an advantage.

• 
Strong interpersonal skills and a service-minded approach to collaborating with colleagues and counterparties across countries and cultures. Experience working in an international organisation is considered an advantage.

 

We offer you employment in a unique organisation, where you will get experience working in an international business environment. The position is based in our headquarter Østbanegade 135, 2100 Copenhagen Ø.

Please submit your application as soon as possible and no later than 18 November. We conduct interviews on a rolling basis.

jobs.occupation: Head of Commercial Products
jobs.employer_name: Impact Fund Denmark (tidl. Investeringsfonden for Udviklingslande)
jobs.description:
As Head of Commercial Products at Impact Fund Denmark, you will turn investment ideas and investor requirements into commercially viable funds and other investment products. You will build the financial models and fund structures that enable Impact Fund Denmark to attract additional private capital for investments in developing and emerging markets.

You will take responsibility for financial structuring and product development, combining hands-on modelling with a visible role in investor discussions. Working closely with the Head of Investor Relations, you will explain product economics, support fundraising and contribute technical expertise to the ongoing investor dialogue for existing funds.

The role is part of Legal, Compliance and Commercial (LCC), led by Frederik Bjørn, General Counsel & Chief Commercial Officer. LCC brings together Legal Corporate, Legal Transactions, Compliance (Non-Financial Risk), and Sales and Investor Relations and consists of around 15 colleagues across Copenhagen and IFDK’s international locations.

You will work in a highly collaborative environment, with close interaction across Investor Relations, Legal, Risk and the wider investment organisation. The team values openness, constructive challenge and strong professional collaboration. You will have considerable ownership of your area while drawing on specialist expertise from colleagues across LCC, Investment, Finance, Risk, Valuation and Strategy & Business Development.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• 
Design and structure investment products, including tranches with different risk and return profiles, risk-sharing arrangements and guarantees.

• 
Build and challenge financial models using cash-flow analysis, scenarios and simulations, including Monte Carlo methods, to assess outcomes for investors and IFDK.

• 
Assess how funds and products work together, including risk allocation and the implications of different investment and guarantee structures.

• 
Develop fee and pricing models that reflect the economics of each product and the resources required to manage it.

• 
Develop investor and sales materials and present products alongside the Head of Investor Relations, explaining structures, risks and returns and answering product-specific questions in investor due diligence.

• 
Contribute financial analysis to information memoranda and ongoing investor reporting, and participate in Limited Partner Advisory Committee (LPAC) meetings and other investor fora for existing funds.

• 
Work with Investment, Finance, Legal, Risk and Valuation colleagues to translate investor and guarantee requirements into clear responsibilities and processes throughout fund and product lifecycles.

YOUR FIRST YEAR

• 
A consistent approach to financial modelling and clear investor materials supports product design, fundraising and ongoing investor dialogue.

• 
Structuring and pricing options for priority products have been assessed, with clear recommendations on risk allocation and economics.

• 
Responsibilities and handovers for key investor and guarantee requirements are agreed with the relevant teams.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

You bring substantial experience in financial structuring and investment products, with the commercial judgement and credibility to take ownership and engage directly with institutional and other private investors. You have:

• 
A relevant master’s degree in finance, economics or a related discipline with a strong quantitative foundation.

• 
Experience personally building financial models and developing or structuring investment products.

• 
A strong understanding of risk, return, cash flows and how financial structures allocate outcomes between different investors.

• 
Experience working with institutional investors, supporting institutional clients or working on the investment side of a pension company.

• 
Experience presenting complex financial topics to investors or institutional clients, with the ability to turn analysis into clear recommendations and respond confidently to technical questions.

• 
Strong written and spoken Danish and English.

You combine technical depth with commercial judgement, take ownership of detailed work and collaborate effectively across specialist functions. Experience with illiquid assets or private-market fund structures would be an advantage.

WHERE THE ROLE SITS

Based in Copenhagen, you will report directly to Frederik Bjørn, General Counsel & Chief Commercial Officer, and work closely with the Head of Investor Relations. You will have analytical support from Strategy & Business Development for product development and investor-related work.

WHY JOIN US

You will shape how IFDK combines institutional investor requirements, financial returns and impact. The role offers ownership of product development, direct exposure to investors and broad collaboration across IFDK, with the opportunity to see your work through from financial design to fundraising and ongoing investor reporting.

PRACTICAL DETAILS

Location: Copenhagen | Position: Full-time | Start date: By agreement

Please apply through IFDK’s recruitment platform with your CV and a short application explaining your interest in the role and relevant experience.

jobs.description:
Impact Fund Denmark - Copenhagen, with regional responsibilities

Help build and operate the organisation behind the impact

At Impact Fund Denmark, we invest in businesses that improve lives and strengthen societies across the world. We are looking for a Head of People Operations and Workplace to ensure that our people, workplaces and operational foundations enable our colleagues to do their best work every day.

This newly created role sits at the intersection of People & Culture, Facilities, Workplace Experience, Governance and Operational Excellence.

Your work will span our Copenhagen headquarters and our regional offices across Africa, Asia and Latin America.

You will report to the Head of People & Culture and work closely with our current team of HR specialists and partners. You will lead a team of three employees supporting day-to-day HR operations, administration and workplace services.

If you thrive on creating structure, scaling services and improving employee experiences, this could be the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. The role reflects IFDK's increasing focus on operational excellence, facilities management and people operations.

You will have overall responsibility for:

• 
HR Operations and employee lifecycle management

• 
Using and further developing our HR systems, CatalystOne and mTime, to deliver efficient, reliable HR services

• 
Facilities, workplace services and office operations in Copenhagen

• 
Coordination and governance of regional office facilities and administration

• 
Process excellence, service standards and operational performance

• 
Vendor and contract management

• 
Global mobility support and compliance

• 
Health, safety, security and workplace compliance

• 
Operational budgeting and resource planning

• 
Workplace experience, employee services and internal hospitality

• 
People legal, legal advice or coordination with legal advisors, internal and external

Most importantly, you will ensure that our colleagues experience a workplace that is professional, welcoming, efficient and aligned with our purpose.

What success looks like

You will:

• 
Build and help run a modern, scalable operations function supporting employees globally

• 
Create and implement seamless employee experiences from onboarding to offboarding

• 
Establish clear service levels and operational metrics

• 
Drive automation and continuous improvement across operational processes

• 
Ensure our offices reflect our culture and ambitions

• 
Strengthen collaboration between People & Culture, Technology, Finance and regional offices

• 
Create consistency while respecting local realities across international locations

Who you are

You are an operational leader who combines strategic thinking with a hands-on approach.

You likely bring:

• 
Leadership experience within Operations, Facilities, Workplace Services, People Operations or Corporate Services

• 
Experience leading small and effective teams

• 
Strong stakeholder management skills, sound business judgement and a focus on value for money

• 
A track record of improving processes, governance and service delivery

• 
Experience managing budgets, suppliers and operational risk

• 
The ability to move comfortably between executive-level discussions and day-to-day execution

• 
Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken

Working knowledge of Danish labour law

You will be expected to work from our Copenhagen office full time on site for the first six months. This will help you build relationships, get to know the organisation and the business, and establish a strong operational foundation.

Occasional travel should be expected.

Why join us?

You will help shape how a purpose-driven international organisation works, grows and supports its people. You will have the mandate to modernise, improve and build capabilities that matter while contributing to investments that create positive impact around the world.

Join us and help create an environment where colleagues can do their best work.

Impact Fund Denmark – Investing in sustainable impact. Enabling extraordinary people.
